90501.text: What are the three basic elements a balloon consists of?

90502.text: What is the fundamental difference between a free balloon and a tethered balloon?
options: A tethered balloon can only rise as high as the length of the rope securing it to the ground
A tethered balloon has no burner
A free balloon may only be flown at night
A tethered balloon is a heavier-than-air aircraft
A free balloon has no basket

90503.text: Into how many types are airships classified, and what are they?
options: Three: non-rigid, semi-rigid and rigid airships
Three: light, medium and heavy airships
Four: non-rigid, semi-rigid, rigid and amphibious

90504.text: What distinguishes a rigid airship from the others?
options: The entire envelope has a framework and the airship holds a fixed shape
The shape of the envelope changes according to the amount of gas inside it
The framework is present only in the lower part of the envelope
It has no engine and moves with the wind
An enclosed cabin is used instead of a basket

90505.text: In a narrow-body (single-aisle) passenger aircraft, what is the maximum number of seats that can be on one side of the aisle?

90506.text: In a wide-body passenger aircraft, what is the maximum number of seats that can be in one seat row?

90507.text: When an aircraft with a capacity of 180 seats flies a distance of 2,000 kilometres, how many available seat-kilometres are offered?

90508.text: On a 2,000 km flight operated by a 180-seat aircraft, 150 fare-paying passengers were carried. What is the passenger load factor?

90509.text: The seat pitch in an aircraft cabin varies within which range, depending on the class of service and the airline's business model?

90510.text: What does the term "aircraft utilisation" refer to?
options: The total block time an aircraft is placed into service on a given day
The total number of landings an aircraft performs over its lifetime
The total number of passengers carried by an aircraft
The net time an aircraft spends airborne

90511.text: What does a runway's designation number indicate?
options: The runway's magnetic heading rounded to the nearest tenth
One percent of the runway's length in metres
The runway's heading relative to true north
The runway's sequence at the aerodrome

90512.text: If an aerodrome has three parallel runways, how are they designated?

90513.text: If the calculated runway heading results in a single-digit number, how is the designator written?
options: A "0" is added at the end
It is written as the single digit as is
It is rounded up to the next multiple of ten
It is expressed with a letter

90514.text: In the CAT II precision approach category, within which limits do the decision height and runway visual range fall?
options: Decision height 100–199 ft, RVR at least 300 m
Decision height 200 ft or more, RVR at least 550 m
Decision height below 50 ft, RVR at least 75 m
There is no decision height, there is no RVR limit
Decision height below 100 ft, RVR at least 175 m

90515.text: According to SHT-OPS, a low visibility take-off (LVTO) refers to take-offs in which the runway visual range falls within which range?
options: Less than 400 metres but not less than 75 metres
Less than 550 metres but not less than 300 metres
Less than 300 metres but not less than 50 metres
Less than 800 metres but not less than 400 metres
Less than 200 metres but not less than 100 metres

90516.text: In the four-letter ICAO aerodrome code, what does the first letter represent?
options: The communication region of the world
The city the aerodrome is affiliated with
The size classification of the aerodrome

90517.text: In which document are the rules and standards recommended for ground handling companies to apply defined?

90518.text: Agreements between airlines and ground handling companies are made according to which standard?
options: ISAGO – IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations

90519.text: In a blended-delivery digital course, how is a trainee's final score calculated?
options: 10% of the pre-test and 90% of the final exam
50% of the pre-test and 50% of the final exam
90% of the pre-test and 10% of the final exam
The arithmetic mean of the pre-test and the final exam

90520.text: Which years does the pilot phase of CORSIA cover?

90521.text: Which of the following is not one of the aircraft exempted from the scope of CORSIA?
options: A scheduled passenger aircraft emitting 50,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually
Aircraft with a maximum take-off mass of less than 5,700 kilograms
Aircraft emitting less than 10,000 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide annually
Aircraft used for humanitarian aid purposes

90522.text: Which of the following is the international standard relating to the Environmental Management System?

90526.text: Which convention did the Montreal Convention replace?

90527.text: Which organisation was established under the Paris Convention and tasked with preparing the convention's annexes?
options: ICAN – International Commission for Air Navigation
EASA – European Union Aviation Safety Agency

90528.text: What does the term "phraseology" refer to in aviation?
options: Standardised expressions that ensure communication is conducted accurately, concisely and unambiguously
The procedure for keeping aircraft maintenance records
The language proficiency test for pilot candidates
The alphabetic coding system used in the cockpit

90529.text: What is the fundamental characteristic of a ramjet engine?
options: It has no compressor or turbine; air is compressed by the forward motion of the vehicle
A turbine produces thrust by driving a propeller
It produces shaft power instead of exhaust gas
The fan and core turbine work together
It produces power using pistons inside cylinders

90530.text: In piston aircraft engines, which type has its cylinders arranged horizontally and opposed, and is used in many light aircraft today?

90531.text: What is the function of the swash plate mechanism in helicopters?
options: To continuously adjust the pitch angle of the rotor blades according to the pilot's control inputs
To keep the main rotor's rotational speed constant
To transmit power to the tail rotor
To regulate the engine's fuel mixture

90532.text: What allows a glider to continue climbing after it becomes airborne?
options: An air current called a thermal
The thrust of the towing aircraft

90533.text: What must a candidate's age be to sit the air traffic controller licence examination?
options: Must have reached 21 and not have reached 30
Must have reached 25 and not have reached 35
Must have reached 20 and not have reached 40

90534.text: What is the minimum English language proficiency required for an air traffic controller licence?

90535.text: By when must flight plans be submitted to the central flow management unit at the latest?
options: No later than 3 hours before engine start time
No later than 30 minutes before engine start time
No later than 1 hour before take-off
1 day before the day of flight
At the moment of engine start
